note: Curaçao, read 2026-10-31. Majority: Curaçao's Civil Code (Book 1, art. 233, inherited from the Netherlands Antilles) wasn't found in a text this client could read (the Government's site serves no copy that was found, and a search turned up Aruba's code and the Netherlands' instead), so majority is null; Aruba's code from the same source sets 18. Work: the Arbeidsregeling 2000, in the consolidated text the Government fixed by landsbesluit of 1 November 2022 (P.B. 2022 no. 123), art. 1 calls children those under fifteen and young persons those of fifteen to seventeen, and art. 18 bars letting children work, paid or not; so 15. Performers: art. 19(2) lets a landsbesluit (a general decree, not an individual permit) take work by children of twelve or older out of the ban when it is needed to learn a trade, is by its nature done by children, or is light, outside school hours and between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m.; no such decree was found or read, so performers under 15 are barred as the Arbeidsregeling stands (a reading to check). The young persons' night and dangerous-work bans aren't held. Service: the Netherlands Antilles' Dienstplichtverordening 1961 (P.B. 1961, no. 223) is still on the books (Curaçao republished its implementing decree of 1964 in consolidated form on 3 December 2025, P.B. 2025 no. 171) and Aruba amended its own Dienstplichtverordening in 1986 (AB 1986 no. 40, found by its title, not read); but whether anyone is called under it now, and from what age, wasn't found: Defence's page on the Caribbean (defensie.nl) names the Arumil and Curmil and the Social Formation Track (SVT) without saying how they are filled, and the Curaçao Chronicle (July 2026) reports a petition against a possible Kingdom-wide conscription, describing only the Netherlands' suspended draft. So service is null.
